name: Jehu
overview: Jehu is a male figure in the Old Testament who was anointed king over Israel at the direction of the prophet Elisha. He is noted for his divine appointment to kingship, marking a significant moment in Israel's history. No tribal affiliation or additional personal notes are specified.
namesAndTitles: The name Jehu means 'y-h-v-h is he,' indicating a connection to the LORD's identity. Another name associated with him is Zimri, which means 'wild goats, sheep; possibly awe of y-h-v-h,' reflecting themes of strength and reverence. These names underscore his role within God's sovereign plan.
familyAndRelationships: Jehu is explicitly identified as the grandson of Nimshi and the son of Jehoshaphat. Inferred relationships include Bidkar as king and Jehoahaz as his father. These connections situate Jehu within a royal lineage important to Israel's monarchy.
scriptureSignificance: Jehu's significance lies in his divine anointing by Elisha, signifying God's intervention in Israel's leadership. His appointment as king fulfills prophetic direction and establishes him as a key instrument in God's governance over Israel. This moment marks a turning point in the nation's history under God's sovereign will.
